author: greystroke
content: Any thoughts on an EIP where Ethereum would retain the existing issuance curve until roughly 50% of all ETH is staked, after which total consensus issuance would stay approximately constant instead of continuing to rise. At the same time, newly committed stake would initially earn only 80% of normal consensus issuance, gradually approaching 100% over roughly a decade. Existing validators do not gain extra consensus power, and withheld issuance isn't redistributed to them. The goal is to reduce incentives for increasing marginal staking without driving consensus issuance to zero or making yields extremely sensitive to the staking ratio. It's largest potential problem is that maturity can create incumbent advantages, particularly for established staking pools and make validator exits economically sticky.
